title: Survival (FM 21-76)
summary: The classic survival manual: the will to survive, shelter, water, fire, food, plants, first aid, navigation and signalling, in every climate.

title: Survival (FM 3-05.70)
summary: The updated survival manual: psychology, planning and kits, medicine, shelter, water, fire, food, dangerous animals and plants, field-expedient tools.

title: First Aid (FM 4-25.11)
summary: Soldier first aid: evaluating a casualty, airways, bleeding and tourniquets, shock, wounds, burns, fractures, heat and cold injuries, bites.

title: Map Reading and Land Navigation (FM 3-25.26)
summary: Maps, grid references, scale and distance, direction and the compass, elevation and relief, navigation by day and night, without a compass.

title: Survival in Cold-Weather Areas (TC 21-3)
summary: Staying alive and working in the cold: clothing in layers, shelters in snow, cold injuries, water from snow and ice, moving over snow and ice.

title: Desert Operations (FM 90-3)
summary: The desert environment: heat and water discipline, health, navigation in featureless terrain, sandstorms, and keeping equipment working.

title: Military Mountaineering (FM 3-97.61)
summary: Mountain terrain and weather, ropes and knots, anchors, climbing and rappelling, rope bridges, casualty evacuation in the mountains.

title: Rigging Techniques (FM 5-125)
summary: Ropes, knots, hitches and splices, lifting and pulling with blocks and tackle, anchors and improvised lifting devices.

title: Foot Marches (FM 21-18)
summary: Marching far on foot: pace, loads, rest halts, foot care and blisters, water and food on the move, marching in heat, cold and at night.

title: In Case of Crisis or War
summary: Sweden's civil defence brochure for every household: preparing a home for a week without power, water and heat, warnings and alarms, and what to do if the country is attacked.

title: Are You Ready? Citizen Preparedness
summary: In-depth civil preparedness: emergency plans and kits, shelter, evacuation, and what to do in floods, fires, earthquakes, storms, pandemics and chemical or nuclear incidents.
